title: Gauge Basics
description: Understand how stitch and row counts affect fit, size, and final project success.

content.summary: Gauge is the number of stitches and rows you get in a measured area with a specific yarn, hook, and tension.
content.whyItMatters: Gauge is what makes a hat fit, a sweater size correctly, and a blanket turn out close to the pattern dimensions.
steps: Read the pattern gauge note before starting.
Make a swatch large enough to measure the center area accurately.
Count stitches and rows over the same measured section the pattern uses.
If your gauge is off, change hook size before starting the project.
Recheck gauge after washing or blocking if the project is size-sensitive.
content.practice: Make one swatch in your normal hook size, then one with a size up or down and compare.
commonMistakes: Measuring the outer edge of a swatch instead of the center.
Ignoring row gauge when the project shape depends on height.
